first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and inherited evidence indicates onboarding simplification durably improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. A guarded test targets a likely root cause of qualified-revenue conversion while avoiding premature broad changes. Promotional pricing is a credible competitive response, but its long-term value and discounting tradeoffs should be checked against the archived record before displacing a durable activation intervention.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment to simplify onboarding. Completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, and two prior records support signup/onboarding simplification as a durable lever: shortened onboarding increased completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and raised 30-day retention 3%; simplified signup durably lifted first-week SMB activation. Promotional pricing directly addresses competitive pressure but is unsuitable for the primary objective because the verified discount test produced a 12% retention decline and failed to sustain through first renewal. Measure meaningful-action rate, onboarding completion, time-to-value, qualified conversion, and 30-day retention by SMB segment before rollout.
